points.text: Sulaiman (a.s) was the youngest of the sons of Daud (a.s) and he succeeded his father.  Allah bestowed judgement and wisdom upon Sulaiman.  Allah also blessed Sulaiman (a.s) with certain amazing powers which are captured in the below verses:

verses.text: Sulaiman (a.s) was taught the language of the birds and was given certain powers. The army of Sulaiman (a.s) comprised of Jinns, men and birds and they were all kept under strict discipline. (Surah An-Naml : Section 2)
Allah made the winds subservient to Sulaiman (a.s), which made a month’s journey in the morning and a month’s journey in the evening. (Surah Saba : Section 2)
Allah also made a fountain of molten copper to flow for him, and subdued the Jinns in front of him by the leave of his Rabb. (Surah Saba : Section 2)
The Jinns worked for Sulaiman (a.s) as he desired: making elevated chambers, images, basins as large as reservoirs and built-in cooking cauldrons. (Surah Saba : Section 2)
Allah said: “O Family of Daud! Work gratefully. Only a few of My servants are truly grateful.” (Surah Saba : Section 2)

Worthy of mention is the incident when one afternoon Sulaiman (a.s) was inspecting some excellent-bred horses (to be used in war). He said: “Surely, I have adopted the love of these good things with a view to glorify my Rabb.” (Surah S’ad : Section 3)
In testing the race of the steeds, when they disappeared from sight he commanded: “Bring them back to me”. Then he began to pass his hands over their legs and necks with affection. (Surah Sa’d : 32)

points.text: Sulaiman (a.s) loved his worldly possessions and admitted it openly. He had a mighty army and Allah had given him some amazing powers. But his love for the worldly things was such that it caused Sulaiman (a.s) to remember the favours that Allah bestowed upon him and therefore to be grateful to Allah.

verses.text: Allah further tested Sulaiman (a.s) and set upon his throne a mere body (i.e. he had a son that was a handicap and undeveloped). (Surah S’ad : Section 3)

Sulaiman (a.s) turned to Allah in repentance and said: “O my Rabb! Forgive me and grant me a kingdom similar to which may not be given to anyone after me. Surely you are the Bountiful Giver”. (Surah S’ad : Section 3)

(It is at that time that) Allah accepted his prayer and subjected the wind to his power, which blew gently in whichever direction he wanted. Allah also subjected the jinns including all kinds of builders, divers and others fettered in chains. (Surah S’ad : Section 3)

Allah said to Sulaiman (a.s): “This is Our gift: you may give to or withhold from whomever you want, without any accountability.” Surely Sulaiman (a.s) has a place of nearness to Allah and will have an excellent place of final abode. (Surah S’ad : Section 3)

Once in an expedition, the army along with Sulaiman (a.s) came across a valley of ants. One of the ants said “O ants, get into your homes, lest Sulaiman and his army crush you under their feet without even noticing it”. (Surah An-Naml : Section 2)
So amused over the ant’s speech, Sulaiman smiled and said “O my Rabb! Inspire me to render thanks for Your favors, which You have bestowed upon me and on my parents”. (Surah An-Naml : Section 2)

story.introduction: Sulaiman (a.s) and the Queen of Sheba

verses.text: Once when Sulaiman (a.s) took a roll call of the birds, he said: “I do not see the hoopoe; where is he? How could he be absent? I will certainly punish him severely or even slay him, if he does not offer me a strong reason for his absence.” (Surah An-Naml : Section 2)

The hoopoe bird arrived soon and brought news about the people of Sheba, who have a woman as their ruler. She has been given everything and she possesses a magnificent throne. (Surah An-Naml : Section 2)

The hoopoe further informed that she and her people prostrate themselves before the sun instead of Allah. Shaitan has made their deeds fair seeming to them, and turned them away from the Right Way. (Surah An-Naml : Section 2)

The hoopoe continued saying that they have no guidance to prostrate before Allah and said: “Allah! There is none worthy of worship but He. He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.” (Sajdah). (Surah An-Naml : Section 2)

Sulaiman (a.s) wanted to verify that what the hoopoe was saying was true. So he sent a letter to the Queen of Sheba wherein he began the letter with the name of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful. The letter read: “Do not be arrogant against me and come to me in complete submission (as Muslims). (Surah An-Naml : Section 2)
The Queen consulted her chiefs to decide whether to confront the army of Sulaiman or to make peace with him. She decided to send presents to Sulaiman (a.s). (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)
When the envoys of the queen came to Sulaiman, he said: “Do you want to provide me wealth? What Allah has given me is far more than what He has given you.” (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)

He asked them to return back, and announced that if their people do not submit, he would march against them with such an army which they would never be able to face, and they will drive them out of the land humbled and disgraced. (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)

Later, when Sulaiman (a.s) heard that the Queen of Sheba was coming in submission, he asked the Jinns to bring her throne to him before she arrived. (Also, he instructed the Jinns to build a new palace immediately). (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)

One powerful Jinn said that he can bring the throne before the court is adjourned, while another Jinn who had knowledge of the Book said that he can bring it in the twinkling of an eye. (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)

As soon as Sulaiman (a.s) saw the throne placed before him, he exclaimed: “This is by the grace of my Rabb, to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful”. He then said to his servants to disguise her throne, so he can test her and see whether she is one who can recognize the Truth. (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)

When the Queen arrived, she was asked whether her throne is like this and she said that it is just the same. She further confessed that they were given knowledge (that Sulaiman was not only a king but also a Prophet of Allah), and they had become Muslims. (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)

She was then asked to enter into the newly built palace. When she saw its floor, she thought it was a pool of water. So she tucked up her skirt, uncovering her legs. Sulaiman said, “it is a palace whose floors are paved with glass.” (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)
At this, she exclaimed “O my Rabb! I have indeed wronged my soul, now I submit myself in Islam with Sulaiman to Allah, the Rabb of the Worlds”. (Surah An-Naml : Section 3)

points.text: Sulaiman (a.s) was a firm believer and an excellent devotee of Allah. However, after his death and as time passed by, a lot of misconception relating to Sulaiman (a.s) started to come up. The people used to associate witchcraft and magic with Sulaiman (a.s). In fact the Jews and Christians themselves talk about Sulaiman as a man who practiced magic and sorcery. Allah clarifies this in the Quran and says that it was the shaitaans that taught witchcraft to the people and falsely attributed polytheism to the kingdom of Sulaiman.

verses.text: Mention is made of Sulaiman (a.s) and that he was a firm believer. But the later people accepted what the shaitans falsely attributed to the kingdom of Sulaiman. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 12)
It was these shaitans who were the unbelievers and they taught witchcraft to the people and falsely attributed polytheism to the kingdom of Sulaiman (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 12)

points.text: The Jinns used to perform magic upon the people and they claimed knowledge of the unseen. When Sulaiman got to know about this, he forced the Jinn to do hard labour as a punishment and he sat there leaning on his staff, observing them, until Allah decreed death upon Sulaiman (a.s). This incident is captured in the Quran and it makes clear that Allah alone has the knowledge of the unseen.

verses.text: When Allah decreed Sulaiman (a.s)’s death, he was leaning on his staff. The Jinns did not know that he was dead (and they continued working) until the termites ate away his staff and he fell down. (Surah Saba : Section 2)

Thus it became apparent to the Jinns that if they had known the unseen, they would not have continued in the humiliating punishment of their task (and it became clear to the people as well that it is only Allah Who has knowledge of the unseen). (Surah Saba : Section 2)
